name: Chia Tao
bio: Chia Tao (AD 788–843) was a T’ang poet.
The poems here are Witter Bynner’s versions, from the texts of Kiang Kang-hu, in The Jade Mountain (1929).

poems.title: A Note Left for an Absent Recluse
poems.author: Chia Tao
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
When I questioned your pupil, under a pine-tree,
“My teacher,” he answered, “went for herbs,
But toward which corner of the mountain,
How can I tell, through all these clouds?”

poems.title: 三月晦日送春 (San yue hui ri song chun)
poems.author: Chia Tao
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
三月正當三十日，風光別我苦吟身。
共君今夜不須睡，未到曉鍾猶是春。

poems.title: 尋隱者不遇 (Xun yin zhe bu yu)
poems.author: Chia Tao
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.note: 五言絕句. Also titled 孫革訪羊尊師詩.
poems.text:
松下問童子，言師採藥去。
只在此山中，雲深不知處。
